:::{#def-surprisal}
#### Surprisal (**self-information**, **information content**)

The **surprisal** of a possible value $x$ of a [discrete random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) $X$
with $\P(X=x) > 0$ is

$$\surprisalf{x} \eqdef -\log \P(X=x).$$

The surprisal is also called the **self-information** [@goodfellow2016deep, p. 73]
or the **information content** [@bishop2006prml, p. 49] of $x$.
Applying $\surprisalf{\cdot}$ to the [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) $X$ itself gives the random variable $\surprisalf{X} = -\log \P(X)$.

:::
